title: Why Afro-Cubans chose music while whites chose other careers
summary: Machito says education was open to all but poor blacks doubted careers; white Cuban musicians like Moises Simons had conservatory chances.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: Correct me if I am wrong. The Afro-Cuban went to music in order like to find a way out of his problem or ghetto.
The white Cuban, /they had everything going for them. /All the businesses ......
what did he do? MACHITO: The white Cuban,

All the businesses, they went to school, that doesn't mean - the only thing that we didn't deny, that wasn't denied in Cuba was education. Naturally, if you are the mind is weak. Because you're poor, poor/that you think why should I be a lawyer or a doctor, where I am going to practice my career.
So the white people, there's no question they are progressive race for hundred, for thousand years ...
Yes, but what I am trying to find out is, not many went for music, right? They went for other things.
No. We got a lot of good musicians that are white Cubans. Entenmann - ah ----
Moise, Moise Simon, the one who wrote......
He was a white Jew, right?
All those people who wrote danzas like eh - a numerous of good musicians - we had ----
All those guys that had the chance to go all the way to a conservatory - a conservatory.
